title: A later lesson must need the earlier one
statement: Claim that a course builds knowledge only where a later activity needs what an earlier part added, so that taking the earlier part out would break it.
detail: The reading project's course standard accepts a sequence only when it names its primary understanding, what each part adds, and a later activity that requires genuine recruitment of that knowledge, and it lists links based only on shared words and orphan lessons as failure signals (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/1.0.0/STANDARD.qmd`, Q014). A source atom behind that standard claims compounding only when removing an earlier anchor removes a later explanatory, comparative, interpretive or decision resource (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/standards/student-course-quality/sources/review-hub/course-insights-d7f57fb/ATOMS.json`). Feedback on the course plans asked for links between units about the big idea, not surface facts (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback3/FEEDBACK_RESPONSE.md`, item 19).
